execution_steps: 1. Confirmed via grep that no existing code inspects Matches module structure at all -- same starting point as Metadata and Resource Data before their respective ticks.

2. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 Translation Candidates module XSD directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xlf-002.bin, schemas/matches.xsd): mtc:matches sequences mtc:match (minOccurs=1 maxOccurs=unbounded); mtc:match sequences optional mda:metadata (0..1), optional xlf:originalData (0..1), required xlf:source (exactly 1), required xlf:target (exactly 1), then any-other content -- source/target both use the XLIFF CORE namespace (imported from xliff_core_2.0.xsd), not the Matches module's own namespace; mtc:match itself declares ref use="required".

3. Checked the existing Matches module test fixture (test_obligation_module_coverage.py) BEFORE implementing anything and found it was already non-conformant: an mtc:match with a ref attribute but no source or target children at all (just raw text 'candidate' directly inside match, which the schema's mixed="false" complexType also does not permit).

4. Added XLIFF_NAMESPACE to validator.py's imports (already exported from ..codec) to reference the core source/target qname correctly. Added _matches_module_diagnostics() to validator.py: scoped to only Matches-namespaced extensions, re-parses the raw XML, flags a matches element with no match child, a match with no ref attribute, and a match without exactly one core-namespace source and exactly one core-namespace target (counted independently, so a match with 2 sources and 1 target is flagged only for the source count).
5. Wired the new check alongside the existing three extension checks at all 3 call sites (segment, file/group, root).

6. Fixed the pre-existing non-conformant fixture: added <source>candidate</source><target>candidate</target> children to the mtc:match element, preserving the 'candidate' substring the test already asserted on and the test's own round-trip-preservation purpose.

7. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: a well-formed match (ref, source, target) validates cleanly; matches with no match is a violation; a match with no ref is a violation; a match with neither source nor target is flagged for BOTH independently; a match with two sources is flagged only for source; a non-Matches-namespaced extension is untouched -- all 6 cases correct on the first attempt.

8. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (421 tests, with the fixture fix already applied, zero new fixtures beyond that) against the new check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 421 passed, confirming the fixture fix was correct and sufficient.
9. Wrote 7 formal tests, all passing on the first attempt.

10. Ran ruff (clean across all 3 changed files), the full xliff suite (428 passed, was 421, +7), and the full 6-format regression (3341 passed, was 3334, +7; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

11. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-001680fe5e3920d7, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
